newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: New NATO partnership body meets for first time.
newsitem.headline: New NATO partnership body meets for first time.

text.p: NATO states and 27 partnership countries met on Friday for the first time in a new organisation partly created to try to satisfy the security concerns of countries unlikely to gain alliance membership.

The Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council (EAPC), which will have a permanent secretariat at NATO's Brussels headquarters, merges the alliance's military cooperation programme and a forum for political dialogue with non-member countries.

Both the alliance's Partnership for Peace (PFP) military cooperation programme and the North Atlantic Cooperation Council were created after the collapse of communism to try and fill a security vacuum in central and eastern Europe.
"It is time to open a new chapter," NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana told the opening session of the meeting in Sintra, Portugal.
The new body is seen as a key third pillar in a new emerging European security order for the 21st century, taking its place alongside an enlarged NATO and a NATO-Russia Council.

NATO states, which are set to invite new members to join the Atlantic Alliance at a special summit in Madrid on July 8-9, want the new body to help avoid creating schisms between those countries which win membership and those that do not. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are front-runners to join.
